facts.raw_span: 20-year history of progressive ataxia
8-month history of 'spasms' in his throat
difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Hypometric saccades
Truncal and limb ataxia
Decreased vibratory sense with inability to ambulate
Bradykinesia and mild rigidity
Palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz
Patient was unable to stop myoclonus of the palate with voluntary use of the palatal musculature
No clicking was noted by patient or examiners
Results of testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 were normal
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

concepts.why: The patient's 20-year history of progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with spinocerebellar ataxia.
The patient's palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz and inability to stop it with voluntary use of the palatal musculature are characteristic of palatal myoclonus.
The patient's progressive ataxia, bradykinesia, and mild rigidity, combined with severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, are consistent with multiple system atrophy.
The patient's truncal and limb ataxia, decreased vibratory sense, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with cerebellar degeneration.
The patient's bradykinesia and mild rigidity, combined with severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, are consistent with Parkinson's disease.
The patient's progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with olivopontocerebellar atrophy.
The patient's progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy.
The patient's progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy are consistent with Friedreich's ataxia.
It explains the uncovered finding of hypometric saccades.
